# Creative Source Catalog

This is a growing, curated index, not a requirement to consult a source on every task. Follow the links and read only what is relevant. The library stores references and concise original notes; it is not a repository for copyrighted book text.

## Workspace references

- `assets/Curse of Strahd.md` is a source reference whose use is controlled by `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and the campaign guide's citations.
- `assets/external-book.md` indexes additional books. Its listed book directory may not be accessible in this environment. Local digests in `.github/skills/dm-craft/books/` can be used when relevant; the `dm-craft` skill explains their scope and cautions.
- Other works can be added when a real task benefits from them. Prefer reliable public-domain or openly licensed editions for reusable notes, and record the edition, source link, rights status, useful narrative mechanisms, and cautions.

## Adding a source

Add an entry when a source has likely reuse value, or when the DM asks to keep it. A source used once can simply be cited in the task response. For a reusable entry, create a short note under `references/` and add a catalog row with:

- Work, creator, edition or canonical URL, and access date.
- Rights status: public domain or openly licensed only when verified; otherwise mark it copyrighted or uncertain.
- What was actually consulted (full text, excerpt, catalog record, or secondary source).
- A few reusable narrative mechanisms and any limits or cautions.

Prefer primary texts and reputable archives, libraries, museums, universities, or folklore collections. If a link is dead or access is restricted, record that rather than implying the work was read. Keep notes in original wording. Do not store full texts, long quotations, or detailed scene-by-scene retellings; do not add a copyrighted work's full text even if it is available online.
